headToHead.voiceVerdict: Tie, the closest it has been. Nav now has moves that survive covering the road nouns, which is what rounds 1 to 3 asked for: the never-wrong ('Some places have been in the wrong place.', 'I have reported the road.', 'Wrong destination, not wrong route'), the fait accompli ('I have already told your car.', 'You cannot change it while moving.') and the weaponised concession ('You are right, so I am taking the long way home until you are less right.'). Those are status tells in Vera's sense: what the character takes for granted is the joke. The round 3 rhythm note was followed: 67 of 112 lines are now one sentence, against 5 in round 3, and the Crumb blur is gone. It is not a win, for two reasons. First, the new one-breath shape is ordinary English ('X, so do Y', 44 lines chain with ', so' or ', and'); it is recognisable as Nav only because of feet, miles and exits, so with the topic covered about half the bank is a generic run-on. Second, Vera's pose cracks on the page ('such a chore being this beautiful', the narrator noting her empathy), and Nav's crack, the X-but-secretly-Y that Monster Prom builds every character on, appears in exactly one line ('The option is greyed out'). Half the top 12 are also fragment stacks, the shape the persona now bans outside cuts, so the best of Nav's voice lives in the shape the rules say not to use.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Ours at the top. The 12 are tighter than Vera's, with a real turn in each, specific nouns (red lights, nine fifty-eight, bypass, bollard, buoyant, greyed out, armoured van) and the punch word last. Vera's #45 runs past its joke, #51 is a speech, and #46, #49 and #50 are help-me prompts with no turn. Below the top 12 the one-breath rewrite has added a new fault: 34 of the 67 one-sentence lines run 17 to 20 words, and many put the turn mid-sentence and then keep going ('...which I know is a personal record, and I have allowed for it.', '...because for once I have not talked over it.', '...there and back and there again, for the cardio.', '...and I will not be taking questions.'). The tag sentences of round 3 have become tag clauses.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar, narrowly. About nine Nav lines are clip-worthy, against Vera's four or five, and 'Do not ask who sat at the red ones.', 'Some places have been in the wrong place.' and 'I have already told your car.' are the best clips in the cast. But Vera's clips get repeated as the character ('my career on not dating losers like you', 'no questions asked. Right?'), while Nav's are admired as jokes. Nav has no line a viewer shouts back at the screen: 'Recalculating.' is the obvious catchphrase, but the rest of the cast has spent it (Dash, Tilly, Prince, Vesper, Maximilian all do recalculating jokes about Nav), and 'You have arrived' is now three stars' line too. If in doubt, the bar wins.

This was the round 3 prescription and it worked at short length ('Sir Quill, in two hundred feet, a full stop.'), but at 17 to 20 words it is the new metronome. 34 of the 67 one-sentence lines run 17 words or more.

ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. Openers max 12 (two at exactly 12), jabs max 10 (two at exactly 10), three-words lines exactly 3, everything else 20 or under. But 9 lines sit at exactly 20 and 18 at 19 or 20: the one-breath shape is pressing on the ceiling.

Not PG-13: none. Darkest are 'All three, one vehicle. I will drive. Do not wait up.' and 'Do not ask who sat at the red ones.', both inside the bar's own register.

This is the best Nav pass yet. Generic share is down from 32% to 23%. The round 3 note was followed: one-sentence lines went from 5 to 67, the Crumb blur is gone, the {played}/{wins} digits, 'You have arrived' overuse (now win only), the pleading, the question and the 'Star,' label are fixed, and most round 3 codas ('Not even mine.', 'Keep the receipts.', 'Picnic anyway.', 'You are welcome.') are deleted. The never-wrong move now has a family of strong lines ('Some places have been in the wrong place.', 'I have reported the road.', 'Wrong destination, {star}, not wrong route, and the destination will be hearing from me.'). Two structural notes for the writer beyond the biggest gap. (1) The persona's tic 2 bans fragment stacks outside cuts, but six of the top twelve lines are fragment stacks; rewrite the tic to 'mostly one sentence, never more than one stack in a row', not the lines. (2) Monster Prom shows the secret Y in every character's lines; Nav shows it once ('The option is greyed out.'). Two or three more lines where the authority slips, still without self-pity, would buy the quotability the bar has. Also worth protecting: 'I was this sure of a route once. A wedding. Then a lake. {rival} looks buoyant.', 'Married. I have already set it as your destination. You cannot change it while moving.', 'You are right, so I am taking the long way home until you are less right.', 'I will route you round every person you know until noon, including your mother, who is on the bypass.', 'Crumb is loyal and very stable.
